description: Reported from the Fight phase (a Blade Champion choosing between Vaultswords profiles against Stormboyz): the attack dialog printed 'E[D]≈8.3' for one weapon and '≈3.1' for another with nothing to explain either number — and no hint that 8.3 is raw DAMAGE, not 8.3 dead models. The dialog now carries a collapsible 'Show damage breakdown' section rendering one table per assignment (ATTACKS → HIT → WOUND → SAVE → (FNP) → DAMAGE → SLAIN), each row naming what it needs, its chance and what is left after it, plus footnotes for damage lost to overkill and for the weapon abilities the forecast does not model. PART A drives the Warboss (Power klaw + an [EXTRA ATTACKS] squig) into 2+/T6 Custodian Guard and asserts the section is folded on open, that the real button expands it, that the chain renders, and that the table's rows multiply out to exactly the E[D] the assignment row already printed. PART B activates the Custodian Guard, whose datasheet offers THREE melee profiles — the same shape of decision as the reported Vaultswords choice — and switches between them with the breakdown open, proving the table follows the weapon and that the high-damage profile is the one flagged for overkill against 1-wound models.

steps.comment: zero CP so no stratagem prompt interrupts an activation

SETUP-ONLY PRIVILEGE: make the Warboss a 1-wound model so PART B's defender overkills the way the reported Stormboyz did. The fixture has no 1-wound unit engaged with the Custodian Guard, and overkill — damage spilling past a model's last wound and being lost — is the whole reason expected DAMAGE and expected DEAD MODELS diverge. Only the defender's wounds stat is staged; every forecast, row and footnote below is computed by the real code from the real profiles. (The sibling fight_one_weapon_per_model_11e scenario stages the same field the other way, setting wounds to 99.)
folded away on open — a player who does not want the detail sees the dialog exactly as before
every step of the resolution chain is rendered, in the order the dice are actually rolled
the three rolls the player asked to see, for the Warboss's Power klaw into 2+/T6 Custodian Guard: WS3+ to hit, S10 beats T6 so wounds on 3+, and AP-2 worsens their 2+ armour to 4+
the auto-included [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapon gets its own table too — it is part of the total the assignments box prints
the table's rows multiply out to exactly the E[D] the assignment row above prints — the breakdown explains that number rather than computing a second, different one
the forecast says out loud what it skips (re-rolls, modifiers, cover, stratagems, and any weapon ability on the profile) instead of presenting a coarse estimate as exact
and folds back away — the section is opt-in in both directions
the activation still resolves normally — opening the breakdown is a read-only view and changes nothing about what is submitted
PART B: walk the resolution dock through so the next activation can be picked

steps.script:
var u = GameState.state["units"]["U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B"]
var n = 0
for m in u["models"]:
	m["melee_loadout"] = ["Guardian spear", "Misericordia"]
	n += 1
u["_loadout_checked"] = true
return n
steps.comment: SETUP-ONLY PRIVILEGE: this roster buys the Guard nothing but Guardian spears, so their section offers a single weapon and there is nothing to compare — while the reported case was a Blade Champion choosing between THREE Vaultswords on one datasheet. Stamp the models with the two-weapon melee_loadout the engine itself writes during loadout resolution (same key, same shape) so the section is genuinely two-way. Everything downstream — grouping, the weapon list, the forecast, the table and its footnotes — is the real code path.
the Custodian Guard section now offers two melee profiles — the same shape of decision as the reported Blade Champion choosing between Vaultswords
the auto-picked Guardian spear (S7 AP-2 D2) into the T5/4+ Warboss

THE REPORTED CONFUSION, made visible: a 2-damage weapon against 1-wound models throws half of every hit away, so its expected DAMAGE is roughly double the damage that does anything. Reading E[D] as 'dead models' is exactly the mistake this line prevents.

switch the section onto a different profile with the breakdown open — the comparison the player is actually making. Weapon rows are driven via select() + item_selected.emit() because synthetic clicks do not land inside popup windows.

the table re-renders live for the newly picked weapon: S5 now only equals T5 so wounds land on 4+ instead of 3+, and the overkill warning is gone because a 1-damage profile wastes nothing on a 1-wound model. Comparing two profiles this way is the whole reason the section exists.
